limits: Illustrative thresholds only; no experiments or data behind any number.
Stack comparison (Table 10-2) is qualitative and mentions 2025 plug-ins/updates without citation; has dated.
SigNoz and Langfuse built-in eval claims are vendor-feature assertions, not tested.
Text of the drift-response paragraph is duplicated in the chapter (repeated sentence block).
Code examples are simplified (KS on four values per sample; KL on three tokens).
practices: Turn every production failure into a regression test and keep exemplar successes as golden paths (Monitoring Is How You Learn).
Distinguish systematic failure from expected nondeterminism with a decision tree: success criterion, rerun 3-5 times, then confidence/variance bounds.
Monitor infrastructure signals and semantic behaviours (intent, tool selection, hallucination, abandonment) in the same observability pipeline as production services.
Route sensitive logs to separate clusters with RBAC and encryption at rest; redact, hash or mask PII at OTel span export.
Extend an existing enterprise logging stack unless you need native LLM evals or lightweight self-hosting (Monitoring Stacks).
Start a span at the start of each LangGraph node and annotate tool name, latency, status, error code, prompt id, token counts, hallucination or confidence flags (OTel Instrumentation).
Annotate logs with span and trace IDs so logs and traces correlate; scope instrumentation to avoid noise.
Run a new agent in shadow mode with a shared request ID before exposing users (Shadow Mode).
Canary at 1-5% of traffic, tag metrics by version, alert on regressions, roll back immediately (Canary Deployments).
Export failure traces from Tempo or Loki snapshots into the test suite (Regression Trace Collection).
Log and trace every self-healing fallback decision (Self-Healing Agents).
Log implicit (rephrasing, abandonment) and explicit (ratings) feedback as metrics and tie low ratings to traces for the eval set.
Detect distribution shift with KS test, KL divergence, PSI and embedding similarity (Evidently AI is named for alerting).

Use a RACI chart so every metric has an accountable owner; share dashboards, tag spans with product context, hold cross-functional triage rituals, and do not hold model latency to a different bar (Table 10-3, Metric Ownership).

R (Responsible: does the work), A (Accountable: owns the outcome), C (Consulted: provides input), I (Informed: kept updated)
